title: Taxing the Rich to Finance Redistribution: Evidence from a Permanent Tax Increase in Singapore
authors: Sumit D. Agarwal; Wenlan Qian; Bernard Yin Yeung; Huanhuan Zheng
eligible_reason: Common dates for all treated consumers: tax1/tax2/tax3 period dummies (announcement 2015M2, tax filing 2017M3; CC_estimation.do lines 25-27) interacted with a high-income treated indicator, plus continuous treatment intensity (elas = period x extra tax amount, CC_estimation.do line 71; DBS_estimation.do). Treatment groups defined by pre-period income; no unit-specific adoption dates. Not staggered.
design_notes: Stata. Credit-card company panel (2014M1-2017M8) and DBS bank panel (2016M1-2017M12), consumer-month, PSM-matched treatment (income > S$160K) and control (S$100-160K) groups. reghdfe outcome dum*/elas* , a(cid yr_month) cluster(cid). Several period dummies enter jointly (dum1 dum2 dum3). Heterogeneity via tri_int triple interactions (Table 3-4). Event studies via xtevent with policydummy = (yr_month > 201501) x match (common date). Redistribution analysis (Table 6) compares low-income brackets with the S$100-160K group at the same dates.
n_adoption_cohorts_note: Announcement (2015M2) and implementation/filing (2017M3) are common to all treated consumers.

specs.exclusion_reason: common dates; multiple period treatment dummies (dum1-dum3); PSM-matched groups
specs.treatment_var: dum1 dum2 dum3 = tax1/tax2/tax3 x treated

specs.exclusion_reason: common date; continuous treatment intensity (extra tax)

data_files_note: DataDisclosure.docx: bank and credit-card data cannot be distributed (confidentiality); data stored at NUS. RandomDBS.dta has 1,000 consumer-month rows x 78 variables with masked IDs (cinmask), apparently a random extract of the DBS file; not enough to rebuild the panel. Credit-card data not shipped.
data_provenance_note: 1,000-row random extract of DBS data (undocumented in README); credit-card company data not shipped.
software_notes: reghdfe, xtevent, coefplot; PSM via logit in *_match.do.
screener_notes: Common-date tax increase with continuous intensity; not staggered.
